BiblicalUsage: I take gᵉbar to mean a man, a certain (one), nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 20 times, and Ezra and Daniel show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that gᵉbar matters because every person bears God’s image, and that settles their worth. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
